documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter check. Says she's been eating more starch since the holidays and moving less with the ice. Fasting 140s-170s. No lows. Breathing at her usual, weight up a pound.

Exam: BP okay. Murmur LLSB as before, JVP up. Trace edema. Feet: intact sensation, no wounds.

A1c a touch higher than fall. Discussed walking indoors at the mall, cutting back on bread and rice. Not changing glargine yet - would rather she not have more lows like November.

RTC 4 months, sooner if sugars climb.

conditions.label: Pseudogout (calcium pyrophosphate crystal arthritis), left knee

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily for 7 days

results.text: Rhomboid, weakly positively birefringent crystals (calcium pyrophosphate)

reports.text: Left knee, three views. Linear calcification within the menisci and articular cartilage (chondrocalcinosis). Joint effusion. No fracture or dislocation. Joint spaces relatively preserved for age.
reports.conclusion: Chondrocalcinosis of the left knee with effusion. No fracture.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, Sunday.

66F with knee OA (L scope ~2010), DM2 on insulin, CKD 3b. Two days ago her left knee became very painful out of nowhere and has gotten steadily worse - now red, hot, swollen, she can barely bend it. No fall, no twist, no injury. No fevers at home.

Meds per pt list. NKDA.

Exam: T 37.2. L knee warm, red, tense effusion, ROM limited by pain to about 30 degrees. R knee cool with crepitus only. No skin break.

Arthrocentesis L knee, sterile prep, lateral approach: 35 mL yellow cloudy fluid. WBC 18,000, 75% PMNs. Polarized microscopy: rhomboid weakly positive birefringent crystals. Gram stain no organisms. Culture sent.
XR: chondrocalcinosis, effusion.

Impression: acute CPPD (pseudogout) flare of the L knee. Gram stain negative; septic joint felt unlikely but culture pending.

Plan: NSAIDs avoided with her kidneys. Colchicine 0.6 mg once daily x 7 days (renal dosing). Ice, rest, acetaminophen. Will call if culture grows. PCP follow-up this week; return for fever or worsening.

documents.title: Call re: ED visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called, was in ED yesterday for her L knee, crystals found, sent home on colchicine. Pain a bit better this morning, no fever. Booked with PCP Wed 3/30. Advised to call if fever, chills or the knee gets worse.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED f/u for L knee pseudogout (Sunday). ED note and fluid results reviewed: CPP crystals, Gram stain neg. Culture finalized yesterday, no growth.

Knee much better, maybe 70% - walking with a cane around the house. Day 4 of colchicine, a little loose stool, no diarrhea.

Exam: afebrile. L knee mild warmth, small effusion, flexes to ~90. R knee baseline.

A/P: acute CPPD flare, improving. Finish 7 days of colchicine, stop sooner if diarrhea. Back to acetaminophen. Told her the crystals can flare again in the same joint; if so call early. Sugars ran a bit high in the ED, fine now.

reports.text: Compared with 3/2021. LV normal size and function, LVEF 55-60%. RV remains dilated with mildly reduced function. RA dilated. Severe tricuspid regurgitation, unchanged. Estimated RVSP 38 mmHg. Other valves without significant disease. No effusion.

documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside Cardiology Group

Re: Joan Hughes, seen 4/12/2022

One-year follow-up for severe TR. Breathing is stable at a flight of stairs; ankle swelling modest with salt restriction. Recent pseudogout flare of the left knee, treated. Weights stable.

Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, furosemide 40, metformin 1000 BID, glargine 18 u, atorvastatin 40, cholecalciferol, acetaminophen. NKDA.

BP 132/78, HR 84. JVP elevated, holosystolic LLSB murmur, trace edema.

Echo today: unchanged from last year.

Plan: no change. Next echo in 2 years if she stays stable; clinic yearly.

Cardiology

orders.reason: Vesicular rash right forehead and eyelid, eye pain

documents.title: Phone Call with PCP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt called first thing. Since about Wednesday a burning, stinging pain on the R side of her forehead; yesterday blisters came up over the forehead and around the R eye, and this morning the eye is red, watery and blurry. Sent a photo by portal - grouped vesicles R forehead to upper lid, stops at midline.

This is zoster in the ophthalmic distribution with eye symptoms. Called the on-call ophthalmology office and got her seen this morning. Her neighbor is driving her. They will start the antiviral and renally dose it; I sent a note with her eGFR. Pt agreeable.

conditions.label: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus with keratitis, right eye

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 12 hours for 7 days
1 drop in the right eye 4 times daily, preservative-free

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside Ophthalmology Practice

Re: Joan Hughes, 67 y/o, seen 3/27/2023 at the request of her PCP.

History: burning pain over the right forehead starting 5 days ago, followed by a blistering rash. No similar episode before, no recent illness or injury. Diabetes and hypertension controlled. Takes metformin and lisinopril among others; NKDA.

Exam: vesicular eruption confined to the right V1 dermatome (forehead, upper lid). Visual acuity 20/60 OD, 20/25 OS. Right conjunctiva injected. Fluorescein: dendriform epithelial lesions of the right cornea. Anterior chamber quiet. Left eye normal.

Assessment: herpes zoster ophthalmicus, right, with epithelial keratitis.

Plan: valacyclovir 1 g every 12 hours for 7 days (adjusted for her kidney function). Preservative-free artificial tears four times daily. Cool compresses to the skin. Return 1 week, sooner with worse pain or vision.

Ophthalmology

documents.title: Check-in after ophthalmology
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called to check on pt. Taking valacyclovir twice daily as the eye doctor prescribed and the drops. Pain about the same, blisters starting to dry. Vision in R eye still a little blurry. No new spots elsewhere. Eye f/u booked 4/3. Reminded her to call if vision gets worse or she gets confused or dizzy on the antiviral.

conditions.label: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus with keratitis, right eye

documents.title: Ophthalmology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside Ophthalmology Practice

Re: Joan Hughes, follow-up 4/3/2023

Completed valacyclovir. Skin lesions crusted. Pain much reduced.
VA 20/30 OD. Cornea: epithelial lesions healed, no stromal involvement. Anterior chamber quiet. Pressure normal.

Zoster ophthalmicus resolving well. Tears as needed only. No further follow-up needed here unless symptoms return; her routine optometry exam can continue. A zoster vaccine series is reasonable once the rash has fully cleared.

Ophthalmology

Here to check in after the right-sided zoster. Ophthalmology notes reviewed (keratitis healed, vision 20/30 R on 4/3). Still some tenderness of the R scalp when she brushes her hair, mild, fading. Sleeping fine. Eye feels normal.

Exam: R forehead healed crusts, a few pink macules, no vesicles. R eye white.

A/P: HZO resolved. Shingrix series in summer once fully healed - she's in. Will schedule nurse visit in July.

documents.author: nephrology

Outside Nephrology Group

Re: Joan Hughes, visit 12/11/2023

Another steady year. Zoster ophthalmicus in the spring was treated with renally adjusted valacyclovir. No hospital stays.

Creatinine unchanged, stage 3b. Calcium and phosphorus within range. PTH 137, within the band we've seen since 2020.

Continue cholecalciferol 2,000 units. Return in a year. NKDA.
